A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research despite the changed title and method name. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: v1 reports original token-classification and question-answering results, layer-mechanism experiments, an ablation, and generation case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds computational-cost measurements and further layer-mechanism experiments in Appendix H.

M1.justification: X-RAG is renamed Tok-RAG. Dynamic layer selection, retrieved-distribution estimation, embedding similarities, and token selection remain the same in Equations 13–19; the rewritten explanations introduce no procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use Wikitext103, ASQA, Bio, Natural Questions, TriviaQA, WebQ, and SQuAD, including the same noisy-retrieval scenarios. The added mechanism experiments reuse existing datasets and task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Logprobs, Uncertainty, Consistency-Lexical, Consistency-Semantic, Standard RAG, NLI+RAG, CRAG, RetRobust, Self-RAG, and INFO-RAG. The new cost table uses the existing Q&A comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 Section 4.1 explicitly assigns label 0 when the pure LLM is correct and RAG is wrong, replacing v1 Section 4.2's broader 'otherwise' rule for differing predictions. This revises the reported protocol without establishing a rerun. v2 also adds memory/runtime evaluation and further model configurations for mechanism probes.

E4.justification: Appendix H extends the existing LLaMA-2-7B/Natural Questions mechanism analysis to OPT-6.7B and Mistral-7B on TriviaQA, WebQ, and SQuAD. Section 4.2 adds computational-cost analysis. These supplement the retained noise-robustness experiment, layer-selection ablation, and six case studies.

E5.justification: The token-classification table retains the same generation counts and p-value ≤0.05 significance markings. Neither version supplies repeated-experiment seed counts or confidence intervals, and the added tables introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Every numerical entry in v1 Tables 1–2 is retained in v2 Tables 3 and 1. New Table 2 reports resource/performance results, including 23.98 GB, 2.24 seconds, and 56.12 accuracy for Tok-RAG. Appendix Tables 4–5 add layer-wise measurements supporting the previously reported mechanism trends.

T1.justification: The mathematical substance of Theorems 1–3, assumptions, and Appendix A–G derivations is retained, including the unsupervised-ICL argument. Moving Theorem 3 into Section 2.3, restating existing findings as corollaries, and changing r(z) to v(z) do not introduce new theory.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a distribution-based explanation of RAG benefit and detriment, token-level prediction through representation similarity, and collaborative generation without training or additional modules. The completion/contradiction terminology and revised contribution list reframe these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds an interpretation of the resource measurements as showing little computational overhead, explaining execution with batch size 2. The existing mechanism interpretation and limitation concerning unevaluated 33B/65B models remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents batch size 2 and identifies LLaMA-2-7B for the layer-selection ablation. However, v1's second-half-token sampling restriction is no longer documented. The retrieval corpus, retriever, software stack, decoding strategy, and baseline implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ding et al. (2024) on adaptive retrieval and Bengio et al. (2000) on neural language modeling. Its positioning against application-driven RAG methods and its connection to ICL theory remain substantially unchanged; the Xu et al. year-suffix swaps identify existing works.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and substantial theoretical exposition are rewritten around token-level harmonization and distribution completion/contradiction. Theorem 3 moves into the theory section, experimental presentation is reordered, and the classification setup receives a separate stepwise explanation.

P2.justification: v1's combined overview is redesigned into separate method and theoretical-derivation figures. v2 adds a resource table and two appendix mechanism tables, relocates the benchmark displays, and changes document styling. The existing layer plots and case-study figure are retained with presentation adjustments.

improvement.justification: Clearer theory-to-method organization, broader mechanism checks in Appendix H, and measured resource costs modestly improve readability and empirical support. The gains remain limited: revised classification wording is not reconciled with unchanged scores, and the cost discussion calls overhead small despite memory increasing from 17.50 to 23.98 GB relative to Standard RAG.
